frames.narration: Raters grade documents for 6 queries from 0 (irrelevant) to 3 (perfect). Three are head queries (80% of traffic), three are rare tail queries. This judged set is fixed, so every ranker is scored on the same questions.
Ranker A (current) and ranker B (candidate) each return a ranked list for every judged query. The metric job compares those lists with the grades.
Count every query equally: A scores 0.60 NDCG@5 and B 0.66, so B wins. But A is better on 4 of the 6 queries. B wins on average because of a few large gains.
Weight by real traffic and the head queries dominate: A 0.82, B 0.70, so A wins. On tail queries alone B leads 0.63 to 0.25. The query mix flips the winner.

Break it: take out one query, "gift for dad who likes coffee", where A finds nothing relevant and B returns a perfect list. A now wins with 0.72 to 0.60. With 6 queries, one query decides the comparison.
Even the cutoff matters: at k = 3 with equal weights, A leads 0.55 to 0.51 where it trailed at k = 5. A small judged set gives a guide, not a verdict.

So offline metrics filter ideas and an A/B experiment decides: serve each ranker to a share of real users and compare what they do. Clicks are noisy (people click the top result regardless), so look at abandoned searches and reformulations too.
